analysis:
MARKET & PORTFOLIO REVIEW: SPY is in a mild uptrend (+0.3% vs SMA50, slope +1.39%) — conditions are constructive but not euphoric. The portfolio sits at 73% deployed across 4 positions. AMP (+3.27%), BR (+3.44%), and MCO (+0.82%) are all thesis-intact with no red flags. NVDA (-2.80%) is worth monitoring: the position is modestly underwater from avg $218.34, now $212.23, but remains well above any reasonable stop level. The AI infrastructure thesis is intact; no action warranted yet. However, NVDA is the weakest link and warrants a tighter watch — if it breaks below $195 on volume, the setup has deteriorated.

HARD TRUTH ON TRACK RECORD: 12.5% win rate and 0.04 profit factor are not noise — they signal this strategy is not generating alpha versus passive SPY. The honest directive is to raise the conviction bar sharply and resist the urge to deploy remaining ~$21.8k headroom unless a genuinely asymmetric setup appears. Most candidates this cycle are either: (a) too extended in their 52-week range (>80%), (b) carry earnings risk within 35 days, (c) show flat or declining EPS revisions, or (d) lack the basing-plus-value combination the strategy demands.

ONE HIGH-CONVICTION SETUP: ADBE (Adobe) stands out as the single actionable candidate. Fwd P/E of 9.60 and PEG of 0.61 are historically cheap for a world-class software franchise with 61.9% ROE, 34.8% op margins, and $9.1B FCF. The stock is at 41% of its 52-week range — basing, not extended — with SMA50 slope accelerating at +10%. Critically, earnings are 85 days out (Dec 9), providing a clean window to establish a position without immediate binary event risk. This is a quality compounder bought at a fair-to-cheap price while the trend has stopped going down. EPS revisions are only flat (+0.5%), which is a mild negative, but the valuation and technicals together justify a modest position. All other candidates with better momentum (ZBRA, NTAP, HPE) are too extended (>80% of range or >20% above SMA50). Energy names (EXE, EQT) have declining revenues. CVNA and HOOD carry excessive debt and volatility. Passing on all others. Cash remains a position — one trade is the right call here.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $265.00 or better; acceptable to enter on a mild pullback toward $260 (near SMA50 support). Do not chase above $272.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Adobe trades at fwd P/E 9.6x and PEG 0.61 — historically cheap for a business with 61.9% ROE, 34.8% operating margins, $9.1B FCF, and 12.9% revenue growth. The market has re-rated the stock down ~27% from its 52w high on AI competition fears, but Adobe's integration of AI into Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, and Experience Cloud is a durable moat narrative. At this valuation, the risk/reward tilts strongly in favor of long-term holders. TECHNICAL: At 41% of 52-week range, price is basing and not extended. SMA50 slope has accelerated to +10% over 20 days — momentum building. Price is only +4.8% above SMA50, well within the acceptable entry zone. ATR is 4.2%, implying moderate volatility with a clean 1.5x ATR stop at $248 (6.4% risk). Earnings are 85 days out (Dec 9), providing a clear runway. Stop distance of $17 on 80 shares = $1,360 risk = 1.40% of equity, within the 1-2% sizing rule.
trades.exit_plan: Primary exit: target $320 (~21% gain) or stop $248 (6.4% loss). Thesis-break conditions: (1) revenue growth decelerates below 8% YoY — signals market share loss to AI competitors; (2) forward P/E re-rates above 18x without commensurate earnings growth — valuation overshoot; (3) price closes more than two consecutive weeks below SMA50 on elevated volume. If held past Dec 9 earnings with thesis intact, reassess but do not sell purely on time. Prefer to hold past 1-year mark for LTCG treatment if fundamentals remain sound. Time stop: if price is flat or negative 60 days post-entry with no technical improvement, reassess capital deployment.
